name: Yale Assure Lock 2 Touch Wi-Fi (US)

radios.note: Yale includes Bluetooth in every Assure Lock 2; the Wi-Fi module adds remote access. Older Yale pages say 2.4 GHz only, but Yale's blog says Assure Lock 2 Touch Wi-Fi models also work on 5 GHz with module firmware 1.0.32 or later.

matter.note: No Matter listing or Yale statement found for this Wi-Fi model. News coverage mentioned a separate Matter module, but we could not confirm it ships.

apple_home.note: HomeKit/Siri through Apple Home. Remote access through Apple Home needs an Apple TV, iPad or HomePod as hub. Yale lists Apple Home Key only for the Assure Lock 2 Plus, not the Touch.

google_home.note: Works with Google Assistant voice control through the Wi-Fi module.

alexa.note: Amazon Alexa voice control through the Wi-Fi module.

smartthings.note: Yale pages seen do not mention SmartThings; with no Matter listing we do not mark it 'no'.

home_assistant.note: Home Assistant's August/Yale pages list the Assure Lock 2 but mostly with a Connect Bridge; it is unclear whether this Wi-Fi model works without one.

hubRequired.note: Wi-Fi is built in. Remote Apple Home use still needs an Apple home hub.

localControl.note: Remote control runs through the Yale Access app and cloud; no source confirms local control.

lockFit.note: Yale says it replaces your deadbolt on most standard US entry doors; sold alone or bundled with Norwood, Valdosta or Ridgefield handles. This record is the keyed version; Yale also sells a key-free Touch with Wi-Fi.

keypad.note: Keypad plus fingerprint reader on the lock.

power.note: Four AA batteries are included, per Yale's store.

summary: The Yale Assure Lock 2 Touch with Wi-Fi combines a keypad and fingerprint reader with a built-in Wi-Fi module, so remote access through the Yale Access app needs no bridge. Apple Home, Google Home and Alexa are supported. It runs on four AA batteries. Yale lists Apple Home Key only for the Assure Lock 2 Plus.
caveats: No Apple Home Key listed; Yale offers that feature on the Assure Lock 2 Plus.
Some Yale pages still say 2.4 GHz only; 5 GHz needs Wi-Fi module firmware 1.0.32 or later.
Remote control through Apple Home needs an Apple TV, HomePod or iPad as a home hub.
Yale also sells Bluetooth-only versions of the Assure Lock 2 without voice assistant support.
